title: A transfer arm in four steps
brief: Press Start and the arm moves one part in four steps, each starting when the sensors say the step before has finished: 1. the gripper closes on the part (until GripIsClosed); 2. the arm goes out (until ArmIsOut); 3. the gripper opens and lets go (until GripIsOpen); 4. the arm comes back (until ArmIsIn). Stop ends the cycle: the gripper springs open and the arm stays where it is. Stop is wired normally closed.
hints: One memory tag per step, each on a seal-in rung.
Each step starts from the step before AND its sensor, and the next step ends it.
The outputs come last: the gripper is closed in steps 1 and 2.

assertions.says: The gripper should close when Start is pressed (step 1).
The arm must wait until the gripper is fully closed (about 0.4 s).
Once the gripper is closed, the arm should go out (step 2).
The gripper must hold the part while the arm goes out.
Once the arm is fully out, the gripper should open and let go (step 3).
Once the gripper is open, the arm should come back (step 4).
At the end of the cycle the arm should be fully in.
Once the arm is in, the cycle is over and ArmIn should be off.

order.says: The arm must not move until the gripper has closed on the part.

invariants.says: ArmOut and ArmIn must never be on together: the arm would not move.

assertions.says: Stop should end the cycle: the arm stops where it is.
Stop should end the cycle: the gripper springs open.
After Stop nothing should move until Start is pressed again.
